title: Auth observability: SLO calibration and audit-sampling study
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Over the last 6 months we have seen several support incidents and near-misses related to authentication/authorization flows (SSO/SAML errors, RBAC drift, and gaps in audit trails). Current SLOs for auth endpoints are coarse (99.9% overall) and alerting is noisy because audit-log volume spikes during deploys and upgrades cause false positives. Objective: run a targeted study and delivery sprint to: 1) calibrate SLOs for auth-critical flows (token exchange, session validation, RBAC decision path) by surface area and customer tier; 2) design an audit-log sampling strategy that preserves investigability while reducing noise/cost; 3) reduce alert fatigue by introducing adaptive thresholds and a short-term alert suppression policy for maintenance windows; 4) document a compact post-incident review template and a one-page runbook for Tier 1 on-call.

Scope: evaluate production telemetry (last 90 days), prototype sampling and suppression logic in staging, and ship SLO updates + alert rules and a short runbook. Work explicitly excludes rearchitecting storage for audit logs or implementing full RBAC auto-remediation (those are follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: SLO definitions for token-exchange, session-validate, and rbac-eval are documented with target, window, and error budget

A staged audit-log sampling prototype deployed to staging that reduces ingested events by >=60% while retaining >95% of forensics-relevant records (login failures, privileged role changes, admin console actions)
Alert rules for auth flows updated in OpsMonitor with adaptive thresholds and annotated suppression windows
A one-page "Auth Incident Runbook" and a post-incident template are stored in Confluence and linked from the runbook
Runbook reviewed and approved by SRE and Security (OK from Priya and Dan)
Dashboard panels (latency, error-rate by flow, sampled-audit-rate) added to Console Observability with example queries and owners
plan: Spike (2d): analyze production traces and audit volumes, identify top 10 event types by investigative value
Design (2d): define SLOs and sampling heuristics (prefix-include, event-type retention, conditional retention for admin-users)
Prototype (5d): implement sampling in ingest lambda + feature flag, add metric exports for sampled vs raw counts
Staging validation (3d): run A/B ingestion to verify investigative recall and measure cost delta
Release (3d): roll out to low-traffic region, update alerts, publish runbook and run a tabletop exercise
Follow-ups: RBAC drift detector spike, long-term archive policy, and KMS-tagging for sensitive audit events
blockers: Need access to raw audit log buckets (security approval pending)
Metric export quota on metrics cluster (SRE ticket created: SRE-1295)
Decision on retention tiers from Compliance (meeting scheduled 2026-03-18)
comments: 2026-02-26 — Aisha: Kickoff done with SRE, Security, and PM. Agreed to prioritize token-exchange and rbac-eval flows. Action: SRE to grant read-only access to audit buckets.

2026-03-02 — Marco: Spike complete. Top investigative events: role.grant, role.revoke, session.invalidate, saml.login_failure, token.refresh_error. These five cover ~78% of postmortem evidence in last 90 days. Raw volume concentrated in token.refresh_error spikes during deploys.

2026-03-05 — Marco: Prototype sampling rules sketched: keep 100% of role.* and admin-console.* events for admin principals; for token.* keep all errors and 10% of success events except during deploy-windows where sampling increases to 1% for successes.

2026-03-07 — Priya (Security): Reviewed sampling heuristics. Concern: need cryptographic tagging of sampled events so we can prove chain-of-custody for audits. Flagged as follow-up: add KMS metadata to sampled payloads.

2026-03-10 — Marco: Deployed staging A/B ingest. Preliminary numbers: ingestion down 64% in sampled cohort, recall for investigation events 97%. Dashboard panels confirmed. Filing PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8342

2026-03-12 — Dan (SRE): Proposed adaptive alert thresholds using rolling-median and MAD instead of fixed-percentiles to reduce false positives during gradual traffic shifts. SRE will own rollout to OpsMonitor.

2026-03-14 — Aisha: Meeting w/ Compliance resulted in tentative retention tiers: critical events 1y hot + 4y cold, non-critical sampled events 90d hot + 2y cold. Compliance to confirm by 2026-03-18. Updated due_date tentatively set to 2026-03-28.
